title: Israel Demolishes Ali al-Taher Tunnel Network, Triggering 4.1-Magnitude Tremor
detail: The Israeli military detonated roughly 1,100 tons of explosives to destroy an extensive Hezbollah tunnel network built over two decades beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in Nabatieh, which Israel seized 'operational control' of on Sep 5. The blast, which Netanyahu later called a 'massive victory,' triggered a tremor equivalent to a 4.1-magnitude earthquake and destroyed command centers, weapons stockpiles and living quarters that Israel says were built with Iranian assistance. Israeli strikes continued the same day on Nabatieh al-Fawqa, al-Mansouri, Zebqine and Shihine, with artillery on Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh, Wadi al-Hujair and Wadi Slouqi, and Israeli forces demolished houses in al-Mansouri, Mays al-Jabal, Bani Hayyan and al-Khiam. Lebanon's army said the continued strikes 'threaten existing understandings and arrangements' and hinder its efforts to stabilize the region. The toll since the escalation began Sep 4 (Friday) reached at least 29 killed, including 12 family members in a single Kfar Reman strike.

media.caption: Aftermath of continued Israeli operations in south Lebanon following the Ali al-Taher tunnel demolition, Sep 10, 2026

title: Netanyahu Reportedly Warns Aoun to Disarm Hezbollah or Face Escalation
detail: U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa reportedly told President Joseph Aoun that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would accept nothing less than Hezbollah's disarmament and would escalate attacks on Lebanon otherwise, according to Nidaa al-Watan. The message, conveyed during a meeting the previous week, prompted Aoun to convene security chiefs to draw up contingency plans and discuss reinforcing army and security deployment across the south, particularly Nabatieh, following resident appeals after the recent escalation. Separately, nearly 400 Lebanese public figures — including legal and human rights experts — signed a petition calling for a stronger army presence in Nabatieh, stressing 'this city does not belong to any political group' amid concern over territorial expansion by armed factions.

media.caption: President Aoun convenes security chiefs after reported Israeli disarmament ultimatum, Sep 10, 2026
